subject: Multipath 500 spike — customer status & remediation plan
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: marta.diaz@novapay.com, evan.cho@novapay.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: [Status] Transient 500 spike affecting some hosted inference requests

Hi Marta / Evan,

Wanted to reach out proactively — our monitoring detected a short window (14:58–15:03 PDT) where a portion of requests to our hosted inference API returned 500s. We immediately opened an ops bridge, applied a routing adjustment to avoid the impacted multipath routing table, and put a mitigation in place (no config change required on your side).

Impact we observed: approximately 1.3% of requests across a narrow path returned 500s; p95 latency for affected routes rose to ~900ms during the window. Based on our logs, NovaPay saw a small fraction of traffic impacted (we've identified your client-id in traces and included a few anonymized samples attached).

What we did in the first hour:
- Identified a multipath divergence in the request router that caused an invalid backend handoff.
- Rolled back the routing rule and restored normal pathing at 15:03 PDT.
- Activated prefix cache warmup to limit cold miss amplification.
- Began trace collection and customer-impact validation.

Next steps from our side:
- Full postmortem and root cause analysis (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- If you observed any production impact you’d like us to correlate, please reply with timestamps or request-ids and we’ll prioritize those traces.

Attachments: request-trace-20270415-1507.log (redacted), error-sample-500.json

Apologies for the disruption. We’ll follow up with a detailed RCA and, if applicable, a proposed service credit.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Thanks for the quick heads up, Laura.

We saw a small bump in errors (a few 500s logged in our sidecar between 14:59:30 and 15:02:10). No customer-facing outages reported yet, but our fraud-scoring pipeline had a handful of retries which increased job latency.

Two asks from us: 1) once you have the RCA, please highlight if this is something we should block on for our go-live next Wednesday; 2) can you confirm whether request-level retries from our side will be treated as billable tokens if they hit 500 vs returning a normal generation? We track token-based billing closely.

-Marta

Quick update for the thread —

Root cause (prelim): a transient multipath routing divergence that sent a small fraction of requests to a legacy backend path which returns 500s for the new model signatures. The routing table change was rolled back within ~5 minutes, and we validated there were no lingering error rates after 15:03 PDT.

Billing/credits: our billing policy is to not bill for requests that fail with server 5xx responses originating from the platform. For single-request retries triggered by a customer SDK that resulted in successful subsequent responses, we will not charge the failed token attempt — we will issue a targeted credit for the request-ids traced in the attached file.

Customer comms (attached draft): I drafted a brief customer-facing note for NovaPay (attached as proposed-credit-draft.pdf). Marissa / Ben — please review tone and the credit amount suggestion (we propose a targeted credit equal to the failed requests for the impacted window; math shown in the doc).

I will follow up with the full postmortem doc (link to be published to the status page and shared as an editable doc) by EOD tomorrow.

Neha Kapoor
